rationale:
Evidence from iteration 3 (wide span, x = ±0.07 m): line_loss_events fell from 1 to 0 on every track, so the narrow-span line-loss hypothesis is supported. The robot still left the track in all 60 trials, with max_error 0.0607 to 0.0629 and 0 finishes. The failure has moved from line loss to lateral excursion just past the 0.06 m limit. Progress is poor and early: s-bend 0.042 and slalom 0.035, which is about the first 0.2 m of the course. Oval reached 0.188 on average. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Even at body_width 0.18 that is 0.0575, so widening the body cannot help. The limit has to be cleared by keeping lateral error below 0.06 m.

Decision: keep the wide sensor span, since it removed line loss, and make one controller change. I am lowering base_speed from 1.4 to 1.1. Early failure at the same point on all tracks, with no change from kp 3.0 to 2.0 or ki 0 to 0.4, points to a speed-dependent transient, such as yaw overshoot and tyre slip at start and bend entry. Less speed should reduce that lateral drift. The cost is completion time, which only matters once the robot stays on the line. The other gains stay fixed (kp 2.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.15) so this race isolates speed.

Expected result: max_error falls below 0.06 on s-bend and slalom, off_track endings fall, and progress rises well above 0.14 on at least one track. Hypothesis to test: the dominant error is speed-driven. If max_error stays at about 0.061 at speed 1.1, the cause is not speed, and the next test is sensor y placement (moving the array closer to the axle, y about 0.02) or kd.
